calls.reason: Cambridge/Science index shows fake accounts at ~8-12 cents; exposed AI networks (Doublespeed, Claude-run ops) drew only labels or bans. The Latvian SIMcartel arrests concern fraud infrastructure, not political swarms.
Largely rhetorical causal claim. NATO StratCom shows cheap fake engagement but also rising removals, and no study links pennies-cost, rapid personas, and successful manipulation together.
Open-ended forecast with no deadline; the only 2026 case (Anthropic's Malaysia network) was rated Breakout Category Two, showing swarms exist but not that they are worse.
Alethea found LLM-varied text made detection harder, but Citizen Lab's 2025 AI-enabled network was still flagged partly by identical content; mixed evidence for an absolute 'no longer works'.
Zurich Reddit bots tailored persuasive replies and Anthropic's network sought long-term engagement, but posts were human-reviewed and no evidence shows real-time machine-speed adaptation.
The only in-period study (Foerster et al.) finds reasoning models often recover from poisoning, and no audit tests reasoning models against web-scale grooming.
